<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>app</artifactId>
    <version>0.1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.release>25</maven.compiler.release>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
        <lombok.version>1.18.48</lombok.version>
        <junit.version>5.13.4</junit.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- Compile-time only: generates getters, setters, constructors, builders, etc. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
            <artifactId>lombok</artifactId>
            <version>${lombok.version}</version>
            <scope>provided</scope>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.14.0</version>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- JDK 23+ no longer runs annotation processors implicitly, so register Lombok explicitly. -->
                    <annotationProcessorPaths>
                        <path>
                            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
                            <artifactId>lombok</artifactId>
                            <version>${lombok.version}</version>
                        </path>
                    </annotationProcessorPaths>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.3</version>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>
EOF
cat > lombok.config <<'EOF'
# Stop Lombok config lookup from walking above the project root.
config.stopBubbling = true
# Mark generated code so coverage tools (JaCoCo) and static analysis ignore it.
lombok.addLombokGeneratedAnnotation = true
EOF
cat > src/main/java/com/example/model/User.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.model;

import lombok.AllArgsConstructor;
import lombok.Builder;
import lombok.Data;
import lombok.NoArgsConstructor;

/**
 * Example entity: {@code @Data} generates getters, setters, equals/hashCode and toString;
 * the constructor annotations and {@code @Builder} cover object creation.
 */
@Data
@Builder
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
public class User {
    private Long id;
    private String name;
    private String email;
}
EOF
cat > src/test/java/com/example/model/UserTest.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.model;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class UserTest {

    @Test
    void lombokGeneratesAccessorsConstructorsAndBuilder() {
        User built = User.builder().id(1L).name("Ada").email("ada@example.com").build();
        User constructed = new User(1L, "Ada", "ada@example.com");

        User mutable = new User();
        mutable.setId(1L);
        mutable.setName("Ada");
        mutable.setEmail("ada@example.com");

        assertEquals("Ada", built.getName());
        assertEquals(built, constructed);
        assertEquals(built, mutable);
    }
}
EOF
cat > .gitignore <<'EOF'
target/
*.class
.idea/
*.iml
.vscode/
.classpath
.project
.settings/
EOF
mvn -q -B test 2>&1 | tail -30

content.text:
I set up a Maven project in `/work` that uses **Lombok** to generate getters, setters and constructors. `mvn test` passes: one test confirms that the generated getters, setters, constructors and builder all work.

**Files:**
- `pom.xml`
  - Targets Java 25 and uses Lombok 1.18.48 (the latest release) with `provided` scope, so it's only used at compile time and doesn't ship with the app.
  - JUnit 5 is included for tests.
  - Lombok is registered in `annotationProcessorPaths`. This is required: since JDK 23, Java no longer runs annotation processors automatically, so without it Lombok fails without any error. The installed JDK is 26.
- `lombok.config`: stops Lombok from picking up config files from parent folders, and marks generated code so coverage tools like JaCoCo skip it.
- `src/main/java/com/example/model/User.java`: an example class using `@Data` (getters, setters, `equals`/`hashCode`, `toString`), `@NoArgsConstructor`, `@AllArgsConstructor` and `@Builder`.
- `src/test/java/com/example/model/UserTest.java`: the test that uses all of those.
- `.gitignore`: ignores Maven and IDE files.

**Notes for the team:**
- **IDE:** IntelliJ supports Lombok out of the box, but annotation processing must be turned on. VS Code and Eclipse need the Lombok extension or plugin.
- **Build warning:** on JDK 26, Lombok prints a `sun.misc.Unsafe` deprecation warning during the build. It's harmless for now, but it's worth keeping Lombok up to date as the JDK changes.
- **Records:** for simple read-only data classes, Java `record`s give you constructors, getters and `equals` with no library at all. Lombok earns its place for mutable classes, builders and JPA entities.
- **Entities:** don't put `@Data` on JPA entities. Use `@Getter`/`@Setter` instead, because the generated `equals`/`hashCode` causes problems with lazy loading.

Nothing has been committed yet.
